newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil stops output at N.Sea Yme oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Statoil stops output at N.Sea Yme oilfield.

text.p: Oil production at the North Sea Yme field was suspended on Thursday due to problems with the mooring system of the submerged turret loading system (STL), operator Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil ) said.
Output was expected to remain shut in for up to seven days, Statoil said.
Yme, the smallest independent field to be developed on the Norwegian continental shelf, pumped an average 38,000 barrels per day in April.
Statoil said a routine inspection found that four of eight connecting link bolts attached to the STL buoy were out of position.
The Polysaga tanker is permanently moored to the STL buoy, with oil being transferred from the storage ship to shuttle tankers for delivery.
Polysaga is due to disconnect from the loading system and sail to the Mongstad terminal near Bergen with a full cargo at the end of the week, Statoil said.
